evidenceBoundary: The two ONNX registry calls and adopted argument/program comparisons are fake-native-executed and statically tied to the fixed upstream implementation. No new official host was authorized, so M10 remains runtime-deferred. Shape equality remains planned and has no fake-native execution claim.

mappings.ownership: the native size is copied by value; no native pointer or registry lifetime escapes the call
mappings.decisionRationale: A bounded managed count is required to allocate an independent read-only parser-name snapshot and can fail closed on size_t overflow or count drift.

mappings.ownership: each borrowed const-backed char pointer is decoded with strict UTF-8 and deep-copied before the native call scope ends
mappings.decisionRationale: The fixed implementation indexes a process-lifetime sorted vector and returns c_str(); immediate copying provides a safe managed capability hint without exposing borrowed memory.

mappings.ownership: MIGraphXShape remains an immutable managed snapshot with no retained native owner or disposal contract
mappings.decisionRationale: The native comparison covers type, static lengths/strides or dynamic ranges, and tuple sub-shapes, but the current managed value already exposes its supported snapshot fields.
mappings.notAdoptedReason: Calling the C entry point would require temporary native materialization or a new retained handle with no additional supported value, and would weaken the existing owner-free value-object contract.

mappings.ownership: two host-backed owned arguments remain alive under a stable owner-id lock order; no buffer or handle ownership transfers
mappings.decisionRationale: The fixed raw_data comparison treats two native empty values as equal; otherwise it compares shape, then logical computable tensor views or non-computable byte views. Public arguments are owned non-empty host copies, so this provides an explicit exact content comparison without exposing the native empty form.

mappings.ownership: two owned programs remain alive under a stable owner-id lock order; comparison neither mutates nor transfers either handle
mappings.decisionRationale: ROCm 7.2.1 compares program print strings; an explicitly named version-bound structural comparison is useful when documented as narrower than model hash or semantic equivalence.
